I adore the Nicolas Flamel series; the alchemist, sorceress, necromancer etc. I'd love to emerge myself in another world as exciting and stimulating. Any recommendations?
His Shannara series was pretty good when I read it and seems to be his most popular. My favorite of his, however, were his Magic Kingdom on Landover series.
The original sword of Shanara trilogy was awesome, I can still see the landscapes and characters in my mind and I first read them 20 years ago. The Scions of Shanara books (4) were also very cool.

Countless years in the future. Earth split into different planets. Humans. Elves. Dwarves. Hardcore magic. Dragons. Death labyrinth. Amazing characters you will fall in love with and carry with you even after you finish the series. Seven books in all.
I second this. Loved the series! Now I need to track down my old copies and reread them.
You forget so much--revisiting them is always great for me. Haplo is my most favorite character in all books. I really feel like the series is Weis and Hickman's crowning jewel.

• The Gentleman Bastard series by Scott Lynch - A wonderfully realized fantasy world with the primary story following the adventures of Locke Lamora, a master thief who pits himself against the aristocracy, magic users and even other thieves. Three books in the series so far with more planned.

  • The Kingkiller Chronicles by Patrick Rothfuss - Kovothe is one of the most notorious and powerful men in the world. Several years ago he mysteriously disappeared however he has been tracked down by a Chronicler who wants to hear his story in his own words. Styled as Kvothe telling his story from being orphaned by the evil Chandarian as a child through his many adventures this series is a must read. Two books in the series so far with one more being written now.
Thank you so much! I think I'll try the gentlemen bastard first because I've never actually heard of the series and then I'll get around to the kingkiller. Need some books for the beach.

The Gentlemen Bastard series is definitely an excellent one. You really begin to feel for the characters and it's an extremely well fleshed out world in the best kind of way, the author just jumps right in without giving loads of backstory or explanation first.

The Book of Swords series by Fred Saberhagen. I read them as a teenager when I got them from a book club. The world in the books was wonderful, you get attached to the characters, both good and bad, and it sums up nicely.
